title: The one-element case of lifting a Popescu resolution.
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, $A$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra, $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra map and $q$ a prime of $\Lambda$. Resolution and strict standardness mean [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] and [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. For a list $\pi$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(r)$, require all elements to map into $q$, multiplication by $\pi_i$ and $\pi_i^2$ to have equal kernels on $R$ and $\Lambda$ modulo preceding eighth powers, and all images in $A$ to be strictly standard. The final quotient map commutes with $\alpha$ and its prime pulls back to $q$. For $r=1$, assertion $P(1)$ of [def-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-induction] holds.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: For the unique index of Fin(1), the preceding-eighth-powers sets are empty and their spans are zero. Evaluate each multiplication-kernel equivalence on quotient classes and use the quotient-by-zero kernel criterion. The annihilator-of-principal-span criterion then yields the annihilator equalities in R and Λ. The total eighth-power span is the singleton span (π₀⁸). Unpack the reduced resolution A/(π₀⁸) → C → Λ/(π₀⁸) and its compatible quotient map and prime.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: Apply popescu_desingularize_lifting_apply (07F0) to π₀, the annihilator equalities, strict standardness, and the reduced factorization. This supplies a finitely presented B, A → B → Λ with composite α, smoothness R[1/π₀] → B[1/π₀], and containment of the extended singular ideal of C in the quotient image of h_B.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: Let J=(π₀⁸), K=JΛ, p:Λ→Λ/K, and L=h_B. Smooth.of_isLocalization_Away makes R→R[1/π₀] smooth directly. Identify the scalar tower for Localization.awayMap and use Smooth.comp to show B[1/π₀] is smooth over R. The image of π₀ in B is therefore a generator of the singular ideal; its image in Λ lies in L. Hence K≤L. Since L is radical and contains ker(p), Ideal.map_radical_of_surjective shows p(L) is radical, so the output of 07F0 gives h_C≤p(L). Also p⁻¹(p(L))=L.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: Prove singular_quotient_le for an arbitrary base ideal J. For every a with A[1/a] smooth over R, Smooth.baseChange and IsLocalization.Away.tensorProductEquivTMulRight make the localization of (R/J)⊗_R A at 1⊗a smooth over R/J. Extend from these generators to spans and radicals using Ideal.map_radical_le. TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor identifies A/JA with this tensor product; singularIdeal_map_equiv_le transports the singular ideal back to A/JA. Compatibility of α and its quotient α₀, composition of ideal maps, and map_radical_le yield p(h_A)≤h_Ā.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: The reduced resolution gives h_Ā≤h_C, hence p(h_A)≤h_C≤p(L). Taking inverse images and using p⁻¹(p(L))=L gives h_A≤L. If L≤q, the identity comap(p,q₀)=q would imply p(L)≤q₀, hence h_C≤q₀, contradicting the reduced resolution. Thus the lifted factorization satisfies IsPopescuResolution.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: FinitePresentation.iff supplies a finite polynomial quotient Q over R and an algebra equivalence Q≃B. Take D=ULift.{v} Q, which lies in Type(max u v), and compose ULift.algEquiv with that equivalence. Transport finite presentation, A→B, B→Λ, and the composite equality to D; popescuIdeal_comp_equiv transports the singular ideal conditions. This yields CanBePopescuResolved with the required universe bound. No algebra witness is defined from an unproved existence statement.
